messages:
elle: heads-up — I hit a consistent double-evict during a prefix handoff on canary this morning. seen it twice.

mike: saw a spike in stale-read errors around 09:12 UTC, likely correlated. logs show two separate evict applies for same prefix.

jordan: can you paste a log snippet?

elle: sure — excerpt below. it's tiny but you can see the swap race.
```
2026-03-15T09:12:21Z evict prefix=tenant/abc lease_id= L-42 swap_token=tok-9a prefetch_inflight=1
2026-03-15T09:12:21Z evict-apply prefix=tenant/abc result=ok owner=node-3
2026-03-15T09:12:21Z lease-revoke prefix=tenant/abc from=node-3
2026-03-15T09:12:21Z evict prefix=tenant/abc lease_id= L-43 swap_token=tok-9b prefetch_inflight=0
2026-03-15T09:12:21Z evict-apply prefix=tenant/abc result=ok owner=node-7
2026-03-15T09:12:21Z read prefix=tenant/abc returned=stale
```

elle: my read of it: two nodes thought they could evict/own because the swap ack path didn't serialize; the second evict cleared cached KV unexpectedly.

infra-bot: incident created: #INC-3672 (kv-prefix-handoff-double-evict) — added runbook link.

kate: hypothesis: we don't have an in-flight marker that prevents concurrent completion. we need both safety (no double-apply) and liveness (fast handoff).

sam: quick proposal: add a handoff_epoch (monotonic) on the prefix manifest. owners must provide epoch in their evict/own ack. evict becomes a compare-and-swap on epoch. if CAS fails, the evict should no-op and emit "evict_conflict" metric.

mike: that helps with safety. question: how do we prevent a crashed process leaving a stale epoch and blocking progress?

sam: keep lease TTL + background reconciler that bumps epoch if current owner missing after TTL. additionally allow a "forced reclaim" flag for operator tests.

jordan: production perf concern: CAS on hot prefixes could add latency. can we optimize common-case with a local fast-path and async confirm?

sam: yes — fast-path: optimistic evict locally, but mark prefix as "handoff_inflight" and serve degraded reads (serve-from-disk or tag as stale) until CAS completes. if CAS fails, rollback noop; if CAS succeeds, clear marker. marker TTL = short (50–200ms) by default, configurable.

ell e: need metrics + alerts: handoff_start, handoff_success, handoff_fail, double_evict_detected, handoff_inflight_duration. without them we won't catch regressions.

jordan: can we add a smoke test? plan: a CLI endpoint that forces epoch increments and run a high-QPS swapping loop while running integration read checks.

sam: sketch of smoke script:
```bash
# force a bunch of swaps and assert no stale reads
for i in $(seq 1 1000); do
  curl -X POST http://canary.internal/__debug/force_swap?prefix=tenant/abc
  ./kv-read-check --prefix tenant/abc --expect-consistent
done
```

mike: sounds good. also add a unit that simulates crash-after-evict to ensure reclaim path works.

jordan: I'll implement epoch CAS + handoff_inflight marker in runtime, sam will add reconciler. plan: land to canary branch, run smoke, then canary deploy for 24h.

deploy-bot: deploy started: canary/evict-epoch-fix by jordan (build 3f2a7d) — rolling to 10% nodes.

kate: :thumbsup: please add docs to /docs/prefix-handoff.md and include operator reclaim steps.

mike: agree — also add Grafana panels for those new metrics and a pager rule for double_evict_count > 0 over 5m.

elle: thanks all — let's sync tomorrow 11am to review canary results.
